cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: My guest on the show today is Alice Riches who started the Street Play Scheme where she

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: lives in Beechwood Road.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: For those of you that don't already know – Street Play involves local residents closing

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: off their street for a few hours so that children have a chance to play in the street

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: safely.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: She started it in her own street, Beechwood Road, and the idea caught on, and there are

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: now Street Play Schemes all over the city.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: So when did you actually start the scheme, Alice?

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: Well, I first had the idea when my oldest child was still a toddler, so that's about six

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: years ago now – but it took at least two years of campaigning before we were actually

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: able to make it happen. So the scheme's been up and running for three years now.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: We'd love to be able to close our road for longer – for the whole weekend, from Saturday

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: morning until Sunday evening, for example. At the moment it's just once a week.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: But when we started it was only once a month. But we're working on it.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: So what actually happens when Beechwood Road is closed?

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: We have volunteer wardens, mostly parents but some elderly residents too, who block off

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: our road at either end.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: The council have provided special signs but there's always a volunteer there to explain

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: what's happening to any motorists.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: Generally, they're fine about it – we've only had to get the police involved once or

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: twice.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: Now I should explain that the road isn't completely closed to cars.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: But only residents' cars are allowed.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: If people really need to get in or out of Beechwood Road, it's not a problem – as long as

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: they drive at under 20 kilometres per hour.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: But most people just decide not to use their cars during this time, or they park in

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: another street. The wardens are only there to stop through traffic.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: So can anyone apply to get involved in Street Play?

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: Absolutely – we want to include all kids in the city – especially those who live on busy

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: roads. It's here that demand is greatest.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: Obviously, there isn't such demand in wealthier areas where the children have access to

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: parks or large gardens – or in the suburbs where there are usually more places for

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: children to play outside.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: I'd recommend that anyone listening who likes the idea should just give it a go.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: We've been surprised by the positive reaction of residents all over the city.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: And that's not just parents.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: There are always a few who complain but they're a tiny minority.

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: On the whole everyone is very supportive and say they're very happy to see children out

cues.speaker: OE
cues.text: on the street – even if it does get quite noisy.
